cohort: The study included 82 women with decreased fetal movement at gestational age >=34 weeks to 42 weeks of gestation.
finding: Perinatal mortality was low and still birth negligible in women with decreased fetal movement, but there were increased rates of meconium stained liquor (MSL) and neonatal admission.
mod_finding: Among women with decreased fetal movement, 47.6% had cesarean delivery, 51.1% had vaginal delivery (including 1.2% vacuum delivery), and 35.5% had induction of labor.
